River overtopping.provides: hours to days of forecastable rise, predictable location along the channel

Coastal storm surge.requires: low pressure and onshore wind at high tide
Coastal storm surge.provides: days of meteorological warning, short violent duration, wave action

Flash surface runoff.requires: intense rainfall on impermeable or saturated ground
Flash surface runoff.provides: minutes to an hour of warning, unpredictable location, short duration

Groundwater rise.provides: weeks of slow rise, no flow velocity, no barrier can exclude it

Earth embankment.requires: space for a wide footprint and a maintained core
Earth embankment.provides: large volume retention, vulnerable to saturation and internal erosion

Concrete flood wall.provides: narrow footprint, high resistance to wave impact, brittle failure if undermined

Demountable barrier.requires: people and hours to install before the event
Demountable barrier.provides: no permanent structure, protection only if deployed in time

Upstream storage reservoir.requires: a catchment upstream of the receptor
Upstream storage reservoir.provides: reduction of a flood peak before it arrives, no effect on anything generated downstream of it

Overtopping without breach.provides: flooding while the structure survives, repairable

Internal erosion and piping.requires: a porous or poorly compacted body under prolonged head
Internal erosion and piping.provides: sudden collapse after hours of loading, no warning at the crest

Structural collapse.provides: catastrophic sudden release, total loss of defence

Not deployed in time.requires: a defence that must be installed rather than standing
Not deployed in time.provides: complete absence of protection, no structural failure at all

Under two hours.requires: an event with almost no lead time
Under two hours.provides: time only for what is already in place

Half a day.provides: time to deploy temporary measures and evacuate

Several days.provides: time for anything, including reservoir drawdown

_v1_notes.FLOOD SOURCE|DEFENCE TYPE: groundwater rise defeats every barrier type - water arrives from beneath, so embankments, walls, demountables and upstream storage are all N. A storage reservoir is N for coastal surge, which originates seaward of any catchment. A demountable barrier is N for flash runoff, which gives no time to install it.
_v1_notes.FLOOD SOURCE|FAILURE MODE: flash runoff is N for internal erosion, which requires hours of sustained head. Groundwater rise produces no failure mode other than overtopping in the loosest sense - piping, collapse and non-deployment all presuppose a barrier doing work, which none is.
_v1_notes.FLOOD SOURCE|WARNING TIME: river and coastal events are N under two hours - both are forecastable well ahead. Flash runoff is N at half a day and several days, being definitionally short-notice. Groundwater rise is N at both short horizons, developing over weeks.
_v1_notes.DEFENCE TYPE|FAILURE MODE: only a demountable barrier can fail by not being deployed, so N for the other three. Internal erosion requires a porous body, so it is Y for an earth embankment and N for a concrete wall, a demountable and a reservoir dam treated as a control structure here.
_v1_notes.DEFENCE TYPE|WARNING TIME: a demountable barrier is N under two hours - it cannot be installed in the time. Upstream storage is N under two hours and N at half a day: reservoir drawdown to create capacity takes longer than that.
_v1_notes.FAILURE MODE|WARNING TIME: not-deployed-in-time is N when there were several days of warning, since the failure is definitionally one of insufficient lead time or organisation.
